key_insight: Real patient-chatbot conversations vary far more than idealized test cases, and that variation can change how LLM-based triage systems judge urgency.
clinical_relevance: Chatbot and triage tools should be designed and evaluated to handle diverse communication styles, emotions, and conversational strategies to avoid uneven performance and potential health disparities.
method: Analyzed 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations to map communication diversity.
Built a patient simulator that models clinical content, emotion, strategy, and communication style separately.
Tested four LLMs on 1,164 clinician-graded cases using five patient personae.
evidence_signal: In a realism test with 15 human graders, simulated conversations were nearly indistinguishable from real ones, with graders achieving only 55% accuracy.
watch_item: Results come from specific chatbot and grading settings, so real-world deployment still needs careful validation across populations, languages, and use cases.
paper_title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
